newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Dickson map plan acquisitions - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Dickson map plan acquisitions - analysts.

text.p: Dickson Concepts (International) Ltd could be set to embark on a shopping spree for more luxury firms or brands following its announcement on Wednesday it would list a unit in Paris, analysts said.

The Hong Kong-based retailer said it would list its S.T. Dupont subsidiary on the Paris stock exchange in early December. Initial market capitalisation would be about HK$1.7 billion to HK$1.8 billion.
Dickson said it already had net cash in hand of HK$700 million.
"I wouldn't be surprised if they already knew what to acquire ahead of target," said Tara Osborough, analyst at Asia Equity.
Although she did not specify potential targets, Osborough said any acquisition likely would be in the United States where Dickson does not have a presence.
"I know that's where they'd prefer to go into," she said.
Another retail analyst, Kate Newman-Mack from Kleinwort Benson, said Dickson would be likely to spend the money on buying more troubled luxury good manufacturers in Europe and retailers in general.

"They are very good managers. They are routinely offered poorly managed, troubled and bankrupt companies, retailers and manufacturers, " Newman-Mack said. "When they find the right company, they will buy them."

Osborough said U.S. upmarket department store chain Barney's was unlikely to be on a Dickson shopping list. Newspaper reports have said Dickson made an offer of between US$300 million to US$400 million for the store.
Osborough said competition for Barney's was heating up and might make the troubled New York-based retailer too expensive.
"I don't think Barney's would be the one because it looks like the competition is heating up. Dickson's strategy is normally to go in there to buy something cheap and turn them around," she said.
Newman-Mack said it would be safer for Dickson Concepts to keep the money because the company had many expansion plans this year.
Dickson is planning a second Seibu store in Hong Kong, will expand its Escada AG boutiques in Asia and opened the first Harvey Nichols store outside London last month.
